```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

raw_data <- read_csv("GA Gopher Frog locations through 2024.csv")

```
```{r}
Unconfirmed <- raw_data %>%
  select(
    `Confirmed Habitat`,
    year.found,
    Latitude,
    Longitude,
    Site,
    County,
  ) %>%
  filter(County == "Camden") %>%
  filter(!`Confirmed Habitat` %in% c("dip net", "at wetland", "in wetland", "Aquatic"))

cleaning <- Unconfirmed %>%
  filter(!Longitude %in% c(-81.61694562, -81.61695873, -81.61698016, -81.617033))

write.csv(cleaning, "cleaning.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

aquatic_terms <- c("dip net", "at wetland", "in wetland", "aquatic")

ceylon_terr_2024 <- raw_data %>%
  # Camden County = Ceylon; year = 2024
  filter(County == "Camden", year.found == 2024) %>%
  # Exclude aquatic/wetland detections
  mutate(ch = str_to_lower(str_trim(`Confirmed Habitat`))) %>%
  filter(!ch %in% aquatic_terms) %>%
  # Exclude known wetland points (the four Longitudes)
  filter(!Longitude %in% c(-81.61694562, -81.61695873, -81.61698016, -81.617033)) %>%
  # Drop rows without coordinates
  filter(!is.na(Latitude), !is.na(Longitude))

# Total records
n_records <- nrow(ceylon_terr_2024)

# Unique points (Lat/Long combos)
n_unique_points <- nrow(distinct(ceylon_terr_2024, Latitude, Longitude))

cat("\n--- Terrestrial locations at Ceylon (2024) ---\n")
cat("Total records:       ", n_records, "\n")
cat("Unique coordinates:  ", n_unique_points, "\n")

```

```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# 1) Read the full Ceylon wetlands shapefile
#    Adjust the path/filename if needed (point to the .shp file)
ceylon_all <- st_read("ceylon_all.shp")

wetland_ids <- wetland %>%
  mutate(WetlandID = str_squish(str_to_upper(as.character(WetlandID)))) %>%
  distinct(WetlandID)

# Correct version
ceylon_all <- ceylon_all %>%
  mutate(WetlandID = str_squish(str_to_upper(as.character(`Wetland.ID`))))


# 3) Keep only features whose WetlandID is in your wetland df
ceylon_subset <- ceylon_all %>%
  semi_join(wetland_ids, by = "WetlandID")
# Reorder columns: WetlandID first, then everything else
ceylon_subset <- ceylon_subset %>%
  select(WetlandID, everything())

# Drop redundant columns if they exist
ceylon_subset <- ceylon_subset %>%
  select(-any_of(c("Wetland_ID", "wetlandid")))

# Sanitize column names for shapefile
safe_names <- names(ceylon_subset) |>
  gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", x = _) |>  # replace spaces with underscores
  substr(1, 10) |>                      # enforce 10-char max
  make.unique(sep = "_")                # make unique if duplicates

names(ceylon_subset) <- safe_names

# Write shapefile
st_write(ceylon_subset,
         dsn = "ceylon_wetlands_subset.shp",
         delete_dsn = TRUE)

```
```{r}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Read wetlands (already projected in UTM 17N, good for meters!)
wetlands <- st_read("ceylon_wetlands_subset.shp")

# 2. Read cleaning points (CSV with lat/long WGS84)
cleaning <- read.csv("cleaning.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Add a simple ID so we can track them
cleaning$clean_id <- paste0("pt_", seq_len(nrow(cleaning)))

# Convert cleaning to sf points
cleaning_sf <- st_as_sf(cleaning,
                        coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"),
                        crs = 4326)  # WGS84

# 3. Reproject points into same CRS as wetlands (UTM meters)
cleaning_sf <- st_transform(cleaning_sf, st_crs(wetlands))

# 4. Use the *edge* of each wetland polygon
wetlands <- st_make_valid(wetlands)                 # safety for invalid polys
wet_edge  <- st_boundary(wetlands)                  # LINESTRING boundary

# 5. Build distance matrix (wetland edge × cleaning points)
dist_matrix <- st_distance(wet_edge, cleaning_sf)   # edge-to-point distance


# 6. Find nearest, 2nd, 3rd
nearest_idx <- apply(dist_matrix, 1, order)  # indices of sorted distances

# For each wetland, get the first 3 nearest point IDs
wetlands$nearest_id_1 <- cleaning_sf$clean_id[nearest_idx[1, ]]
wetlands$nearest_id_2 <- cleaning_sf$clean_id[nearest_idx[2, ]]
wetlands$nearest_id_3 <- cleaning_sf$clean_id[nearest_idx[3, ]]

# 7. Plot: wetlands, cleaning points, and edge-to-nearest segments
plot(st_geometry(wetlands), border = "blue")
plot(st_geometry(cleaning_sf), add = TRUE, col = "red", pch = 16)

# Draw a segment from each wetland polygon to its nearest cleaning point (edge-based)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(wetlands))) {
  id1 <- wetlands$nearest_id_1[i]
  if (is.na(id1)) next

  # Find the matching point row by ID (robust to row order)
  idx <- match(id1, cleaning_sf$clean_id)
  if (is.na(idx)) next

  nearest_pt <- cleaning_sf[idx, ]

  # Segment that touches the polygon boundary and the point
  seg <- sf::st_nearest_points(wetlands[i, ], nearest_pt)
  plot(seg, add = TRUE, col = "green", lwd = 2)
  plot(sf::st_geometry(nearest_pt), add = TRUE, col = "green", pch = 17)
}



```
```{r}

library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Read wetlands (already projected in UTM 17N, good for meters!)
wetlands <- st_read("ceylon_wetlands_subset.shp")

# 2. Read burrows (points, any CRS)
burrows <- st_read("all_burrows.shp")

# Add a simple burrow ID if needed
if (!any(c("BurrowID","burrow_id","ID","id") %in% names(burrows))) {
  burrows$burrow_id <- paste0("b_", seq_len(nrow(burrows)))
  burrow_id_col <- "burrow_id"
} else {
  burrow_id_col <- intersect(names(burrows), c("BurrowID","burrow_id","ID","id"))[1]
}

# 3. Reproject burrows into same CRS as wetlands (UTM meters)
burrows <- st_transform(burrows, st_crs(wetlands))

# 4. Use the *edge* of each wetland polygon
wetlands <- st_make_valid(wetlands)
wet_edge  <- st_boundary(wetlands)

# 5. Build distance matrix (wetland edge × burrow points)
dist_matrix_b <- st_distance(wet_edge, burrows)

# 6. Find nearest, 2nd, 3rd
nearest_idx_b <- apply(dist_matrix_b, 1, order)  # indices of sorted distances

# For each wetland, get the first 3 nearest burrow IDs
wetlands$nearest_burrow_id_1 <- burrows[[burrow_id_col]][ nearest_idx_b[1, ] ]
wetlands$nearest_burrow_id_2 <- burrows[[burrow_id_col]][ nearest_idx_b[2, ] ]
wetlands$nearest_burrow_id_3 <- burrows[[burrow_id_col]][ nearest_idx_b[3, ] ]

# 7. Plot (edge-based): wetlands, burrows, and segments to nearest burrow
plot(st_geometry(wetlands), border = "blue")
plot(st_geometry(burrows), add = TRUE, col = "orange", pch = 17)   # burrow points

for (i in seq_len(nrow(wetlands))) {
  id1 <- wetlands$nearest_burrow_id_1[i]
  if (is.na(id1)) next

  # Find the matching burrow row by ID (robust to row order)
  idx <- match(id1, burrows[[burrow_id_col]])
  if (is.na(idx)) next

  nearest_pt <- burrows[idx, ]

  # Segment that touches the polygon boundary and the burrow point
  seg <- sf::st_nearest_points(wetlands[i, ], nearest_pt)
  plot(seg, add = TRUE, col = "green", lwd = 2)
  plot(sf::st_geometry(nearest_pt), add = TRUE, col = "green", pch = 17)
}
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(units)

# --- Require objects from previous chunks ---
stopifnot(
  exists("wetlands"),
  exists("cleaning_sf"),
  exists("burrows"),
  exists("dist_matrix"),      # centroids x cleaning
  exists("nearest_idx"),      # order indices for cleaning
  exists("dist_matrix_b"),    # centroids x burrows
  exists("nearest_idx_b")     # order indices for burrows
)

# Wetland ID column (adjust the preference order if needed)
wet_id_col <- intersect(names(wetlands),
                        c("WetlandID","WETLANDID","wetlandid","Name","NAME","id","ID","Site","SITE"))[1]
if (is.na(wet_id_col)) {
  wetlands$.wetland_row <- seq_len(nrow(wetlands))
  wet_id_col <- ".wetland_row"
}

# Drop units for arithmetic/indexing
D_clean <- units::drop_units(as.matrix(dist_matrix))
D_burr  <- units::drop_units(as.matrix(dist_matrix_b))

row_idx <- seq_len(nrow(wetlands))

# ---- IDs (already computed; pull from existing objects) ----
clean_id_col  <- "clean_id"  # set earlier
burrow_id_col <- if ("burrow_id" %in% names(burrows)) "burrow_id" else
                 intersect(names(burrows), c("BurrowID","ID","id"))[1]

c_id_1 <- cleaning_sf[[clean_id_col]][ nearest_idx[1, ] ]
c_id_2 <- cleaning_sf[[clean_id_col]][ nearest_idx[2, ] ]
c_id_3 <- cleaning_sf[[clean_id_col]][ nearest_idx[3, ] ]

b_id_1 <- burrows[[burrow_id_col]][ nearest_idx_b[1, ] ]
b_id_2 <- burrows[[burrow_id_col]][ nearest_idx_b[2, ] ]
b_id_3 <- burrows[[burrow_id_col]][ nearest_idx_b[3, ] ]

# ---- Distances (meters) ----
c_d_1 <- D_clean[cbind(row_idx, nearest_idx[1, ])]
c_d_2 <- D_clean[cbind(row_idx, nearest_idx[2, ])]
c_d_3 <- D_clean[cbind(row_idx, nearest_idx[3, ])]

b_d_1 <- D_burr [cbind(row_idx, nearest_idx_b[1, ])]
b_d_2 <- D_burr [cbind(row_idx, nearest_idx_b[2, ])]
b_d_3 <- D_burr [cbind(row_idx, nearest_idx_b[3, ])]

# ---- Ratios (burrow / cleaning) ----
safe_ratio <- function(b, c) ifelse(is.na(b) | is.na(c) | c == 0, NA_real_, b / c)
r_1 <- safe_ratio(b_d_1, c_d_1)
r_2 <- safe_ratio(b_d_2, c_d_2)
r_3 <- safe_ratio(b_d_3, c_d_3)

# ---- Final dataframe ----
nearest_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  wetland_id = wetlands[[wet_id_col]],

  frog_m_1  = c_d_1,
  frog_m_2  = c_d_2,
  frog_m_3  = c_d_3,

  burrow_m_1    = b_d_1,
  burrow_m_2    = b_d_2,
  burrow_m_3    = b_d_3,

  ratio_b_to_f_1 = r_1,
  ratio_b_to_f_2 = r_2,
  ratio_b_to_f_3 = r_3
)

# Preview & save
print(nearest_summary, n = 10)
readr::write_csv(nearest_summary, "wetlands_nearest_cleaning_burrows_ratios.csv")

```

```{r}
# ---- Create simplified ratio dataset with Site ----
ratio_b_tof_1 <- nearest_summary %>%

  mutate(
    ratio_b_to_f_1 = ifelse(ratio_b_to_f_1 > 1, 1, ratio_b_to_f_1),
```

```{r}
# --- Map: Ceylon 2024 terrestrial frog locations on satellite basemap ---

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(maptiles)
library(tidyterra)

# 1) Ensure wetlands are available (read if not already in memory)
if (!exists("wetlands") || !inherits(wetlands, "sf")) {
  wetlands <- st_read("ceylon_wetlands_subset.shp", quiet = TRUE)
}

# 2) Make the points sf and match CRS to wetlands
stopifnot(all(c("Latitude", "Longitude") %in% names(ceylon_terr_2024)))
pts_ceylon <- st_as_sf(
  ceylon_terr_2024,
  coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"),
  crs = 4326
) |> st_transform(st_crs(wetlands))

# 3) Build a single boundary to crop tiles nicely
cey_boundary <- wetlands |>
  st_make_valid() |>
  mutate(.grp = 1L) |>
  dplyr::group_by(.grp) |>
  dplyr::summarise(geometry = st_union(geometry), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::select(-.grp)

# 4) Fetch satellite tiles and crop to boundary
dir.create("tile-cache", showWarnings = FALSE)
r <- maptiles::get_tiles(cey_boundary, provider = "Esri.WorldImagery",
                         zoom = 16, crop = TRUE, cachedir = "tile-cache")

# Align CRS
wm_crs <- st_crs(terra::crs(r, proj = TRUE))
boundary_wm <- st_transform(cey_boundary, wm_crs)
wetlands_wm <- st_transform(wetlands, wm_crs)
pts_wm      <- st_transform(pts_ceylon, wm_crs)

# 5) Plot
p_ceylon_pts <- ggplot() +
  tidyterra::geom_spatraster_rgb(data = r) +
  geom_sf(data = wetlands_wm, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = boundary_wm, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = pts_wm, shape = 21, fill = "red", color = "white", stroke = 0.3, size = 2.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE, crs = wm_crs, datum = NA) +
  labs(title = "Ceylon WMA — Terrestrial Gopher Frog Locations (2024)",
       subtitle = paste0("n = ", nrow(pts_ceylon)),
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

print(p_ceylon_pts)
ggsave("ceylon_terrestrial_2024_map.png", p_ceylon_pts, width = 8, height = 8, dpi = 300)

```

```{r}
# --- Nearest 3 wetlands for each 2024 terrestrial point at Ceylon ---

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(units)

# 0) Ensure inputs
stopifnot(exists("ceylon_terr_2024"))

# 1) Load wetlands (Ceylon subset) if not already loaded
if (!exists("wetlands") || !inherits(wetlands, "sf")) {
  wetlands <- st_read("ceylon_wetlands_subset.shp", quiet = TRUE)
}

# 2) Robustly pick a WetlandID column from the shapefile
wet_id_col <- intersect(names(wetlands),
                        c("WetlandID","WETLANDID","wetlandid","Name","NAME","id","ID"))[1]
if (is.na(wet_id_col)) {
  wetlands$WET_ID_FALLBACK <- seq_len(nrow(wetlands))
  wet_id_col <- "WET_ID_FALLBACK"
}

# 3) Make the points sf and put them in the same CRS as wetlands
pts <- st_as_sf(ceylon_terr_2024, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326)
pts <- st_transform(pts, st_crs(wetlands))

# Give each point a simple ID (row index) for joining/traceability
pts$.pt_id <- seq_len(nrow(pts))

# 4) Point-to-polygon distances (meters by default if CRS is projected)
D <- st_distance(pts, wetlands)  # units

# Convert to plain numeric meters for sorting and CSVs
D_m <- units::drop_units(D)

# How many neighbors we can actually return
k <- min(3L, nrow(wetlands))

# 5) For each point, find indices of k nearest wetlands
ord_idx <- apply(D_m, 1, order)  # matrix of column indices (wetlands) sorted by distance per row
if (k == 1L) {
  # keep shape consistent when only one wetland exists
  ord_idx <- matrix(ord_idx[1, ], nrow = 1)
}

# 6) Build the summary table
nearest_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(pts)), function(i) {
  nn_cols <- ord_idx[seq_len(k), i]  # the k nearest wetland indices for point i
  # safeguard for k < 3 (pad with NAs)
  pad_len <- 3L - length(nn_cols)
  if (pad_len > 0) nn_cols <- c(nn_cols, rep(NA_integer_, pad_len))

  # Pull IDs and distances
  nn_ids <- ifelse(is.na(nn_cols), NA, wetlands[[wet_id_col]][nn_cols])
  nn_dst <- ifelse(is.na(nn_cols), NA_real_, D_m[i, nn_cols])

  tibble(
    pt_id     = pts$.pt_id[i],
    # include original coords for convenience
    Latitude  = as.numeric(st_coordinates(pts[i, ])[2]),
    Longitude = as.numeric(st_coordinates(pts[i, ])[1]),

    nearest_wetland_id_1 = nn_ids[1],
    nearest_wetland_id_2 = nn_ids[2],
    nearest_wetland_id_3 = nn_ids[3],

    dist_m_1 = nn_dst[1],
    dist_m_2 = nn_dst[2],
    dist_m_3 = nn_dst[3],

    dist_km_1 = nn_dst[1] / 1000,
    dist_km_2 = nn_dst[2] / 1000,
    dist_km_3 = nn_dst[3] / 1000
  )
})

# 7) Join back any columns you want from the original data (optional)
#    Example: keep Confirmed Habitat and year.found
keep_cols <- intersect(c("Confirmed Habitat","year.found","Site","County"), names(ceylon_terr_2024))
nearest_tbl <- nearest_tbl %>%
  left_join(
    cbind(pt_id = pts$.pt_id, st_drop_geometry(pts)[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]),
    by = "pt_id"
  )

# 8) Inspect and save
print(nearest_tbl, n = min(10, nrow(nearest_tbl)))
readr::write_csv(nearest_tbl, "ceylon_terrestrial_2024_nearest3_wetlands.csv")

```

```{r}
# --- Summary: how many terrestrial points had each wetland as their NEAREST (edge-based) ---

library(dplyr)
library(sf)

# 1) Ensure points and wetlands exist (pts and wetlands should already be created earlier)
stopifnot(exists("pts"), inherits(pts, "sf"))
stopifnot(exists("wetlands"), inherits(wetlands, "sf"))

# 2) Pick wetland ID column
wet_id_col <- intersect(names(wetlands),
                        c("WetlandID","WETLANDID","wetlandid","Name","NAME","id","ID"))[1]
if (is.na(wet_id_col)) {
  wetlands$WET_ID_FALLBACK <- seq_len(nrow(wetlands))
  wet_id_col <- "WET_ID_FALLBACK"
}

# 3) Compute distances (if not already done)
if (!exists("D_m")) {
  D <- st_distance(pts, wetlands)
  D_m <- units::drop_units(D)
}

# 4) For each point, find the index of the nearest wetland
nearest_idx <- apply(D_m, 1, which.min)
nearest_wetland_ids <- wetlands[[wet_id_col]][nearest_idx]

# 5) Summarize: count how many points picked each wetland as nearest
wetland_summary <- data.frame(WetlandID = nearest_wetland_ids) %>%
  group_by(WetlandID) %>%
  summarise(n_points_nearest = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_points_nearest))

# 6) Optional: join with wetland geometry to map or export
wetland_summary_sf <- wetlands %>%
  select(WetlandID = all_of(wet_id_col)) %>%
  left_join(wetland_summary, by = "WetlandID") %>%
  mutate(n_points_nearest = ifelse(is.na(n_points_nearest), 0L, n_points_nearest))

# 7) Preview & save
print(wetland_summary, n = nrow(wetland_summary))
readr::write_csv(wetland_summary, "ceylon_wetlands_nearest_point_counts.csv")

# Optional map visualization
library(ggplot2)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = wetlands, fill = "grey90", color = "grey70") +
  geom_sf(data = wetland_summary_sf, aes(fill = n_points_nearest), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "# points nearest") +
  labs(title = "Number of Terrestrial Points for Which Each Wetland Was Nearest") +
  theme_minimal()

```
